extracted.intended_audience: law practitioners, solicitors, barristers, and law students
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria for choosing or judging legal treatises, practice-books, digests, and examination guides intended for use by practitioners and students. Focuses on practical utility, currency, comprehensiveness, arrangement, and supporting materials (forms, statutes, indexes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usefulness in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "The work will, we think, be very useful in practice"; "a book of a most practical character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on immediate applicability to day-to-day practice — useful in judges' chambers, for practitioners and their clerks; recommended when the book supplies practical information and forms that lawyers will actually use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and exhaustive treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases such as "nowhere has the subject been treated so exhaustively" and "complete ... a more complete law book than this."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable where the work aims to be authoritative: exhaustive coverage of topic, comprehensive indexes, full statement of leading cases and principles; valuable as a library or reference work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-to-date with latest decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are praised for "putting prominently forward the result of the latest decisions, settling the law so far as it is ascertained" and books described as "bringing the work down to the present time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should reflect recent statutory changes and case law; notes should indicate when rules are new, repealed, or modified and provide references to supporting statutes or precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, concise, accurate, and practical notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers note "notes to the rules are concise, clear, accurate and practical"; "a clear, practical, and, so far as we have been able to test it, accurate exposition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary should be succinct, understandable, reliably accurate, and focused on giving workable guidance rather than excessive theoretical discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and accurate index
rubrics_metrics.description: "The index, extending over 378 pages, is a model of comprehensiveness and accuracy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A large, well-constructed index that facilitates rapid reference is a major quality marker for legal reference works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of statutes, forms, and precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Many entries: "With the Statutes, Rules, Fees and Forms relating thereto", "a collection of precedents of Memoranda and Articles of Association", "Appendix of Statutes and Forms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical legal books should append statutory texts, model forms, precedents and templates so users can apply the law directly; presence of forms and specimen documents increases a work's utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise digests/analyses of cases with references
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each number contains a concise analysis of every case reported ... with references to Text-books, Statutes, and the Law Reports Consolidated Digest, and an alphabetical index of the subjects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful digests should summarize cases succinctly, give citations and cross-references to further authority, and organize material so readers can locate subject-matter quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement favoring current law over historical exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is much more important to be able to see at once what the law is than to know how it has become what it is"; editors avoid "useless reference to older cases."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practice-oriented works, prioritize presenting the current settled law and practical effect of decisions rather than lengthy doctrinal history, so practitioners can determine applicable rules quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible to both students and practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements such as "for the use of Students and Practitioners", "It will be found as useful to the practitioner as to the student."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good works balance depth and clarity so they serve as study aids for students and as practical guides for practicing lawyers; suitable exposition level and helpful summaries are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise presentation and good arrangement for reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptors like "succinct code", "well-planned book", "very handy" and "convenient compendium."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should be well-organized (grouped by subject, with appendices and tables), concise where possible, and arranged to facilitate quick consultation in practice or study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful, painstaking research and accuracy of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Praises such as "the result of much careful and painstaking research" and references to "careful and accurate" answers in exam digests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability of statements of law, correctness of citations, and careful editorial scholarship are essential; errors or sloppiness undermine a work's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory marginal notes, cross-references and editorial apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes indicating where a repealed rule is reproduced without alteration or with modifications, marginal references prefixed by 'cf.', and reconstructed indexes and cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial apparatus that explains provenance, amendments, and relationships among rules/statutes (marginal notes, cross-refs, a reconstructed index) helps users understand changes and locate relevant material quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for examination preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many titles labeled as "Guides" or "Digests" for preliminary, final, and honours examinations with comments like "Will furnish students with a large armoury ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For student-targeted works, inclusion of past questions, short model answers, summaries of leading cases and suggested reading passages makes them useful exam-preparation tools.
